meta.description: Frames PTM/phosphoproteomics analysis as three stacked inference layers on a biased enrichment - chemistry selection, site localization (FLR), and protein-level-adjusted quantification with MSstatsPTM - plus kinase-activity and functional triage. Covers MaxQuant Phospho (STY)Sites multiplicity expansion, localization-probability filtering, FLR, motif analysis with experiment-matched backgrounds, diGly/K-GG specificity, acetyl/glyco traps, and KSEA/PTM-SEA.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated identifiers or data. 23 references checked; MSstatsPTM (MCP 22(1):100477), DeepFLR (Nat Commun 14:2269), Mueller-Dott 2025 (Nat Commun 16:4771) and Ramsbottom 2022 (JPR 21(7):1603) confirmed against Crossref; NEDD8 ~6% of K-GG at basal matches Kim 2011. Masses recomputed from element masses: GG = 2x carbamidomethyl = 114.0429, acetyl 42.0106 vs trimethyl 42.0470 (delta 0.0364), N->D 0.9840 / 2.9883 with 18O. Ramsbottom 2022 is cited in a table but missing from References.

practice_boundaries.detail: Research-only proteomics analysis; no output diagnoses, prescribes or triages an individual.

methodological_ground.detail: The core method is sound and was confirmed by running it: ADJUSTED.Model removed 6/6 protein-driven phosphosite calls and 5/5 stabilisation-driven K-GG calls, and recovered 2/3 masked sites. The adj.p<0.05 & |log2FC|>1 double filter gave 9-13% false calls for a '>2-fold' claim at nominal 5% in simulation. The differential-abundance Skill forbids that filter. It is scored under methodology but does not invert conclusions.

code_usability.detail: Positive evidence: the expansion block and the shipped example ran (exit 0). The MSstatsPTM block fails as written on 2.8.1: dataSummarizationPTM(use_log_file=FALSE) trips an append assertion, and data.type='LF' matches neither branch ('object ptm_model not found'). The motif block raises NameError on 'confident'. None is a syntax error, loop or missing dependency. The Skill's Version Compatibility and '?MaxQtoMSstatsPTMFormat' hints lead to one-token fixes, after which all 5 inputs ran. Scored under Code Executability.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness 2: FLR and KSEA/PTM-SEA promised in the description but no code or command; motif block stops at a frequency counter. Correctness 2: chemistry and references accurate, but three MSstatsPTM API defects (data.type 'LF', append default, no evidence_prot), a bogus 'Intensity' run in the melt and an undefined 'confident'. Appropriateness 3: right tools; double filter and missing localization filter in the R path.

reliability.note: Fault tolerance 2: guards for Contaminant and blank Gene names; the 'accept either form' filename comment is not implemented; the phospho-only path crashes on a NULL ADJUSTED.Model. Error reporting 2: Common Errors lists 7 symptoms, none of the 4 failures hit in runs. Recoverability 3: Version Compatibility tells the agent to introspect; stateless code.

performance_context.note: Token cost 3: 294 lines / 28 KB in one file, long taxonomy tables loaded on every request. Execution efficiency 3: linear blocks, but two parallel quant routes (Sites-table pandas vs evidence MSstatsPTM) with no bridge between them.

agent_usability.note: Learnability 3: the three-inference framing is very clear. Consistency 2: phospho vs confident; the comment says 'supply the global proteome' but the code never passes it; class I applied only in pandas; the double filter contradicts the sibling Skill. Feedback 3: Goal/Approach per block and 'report three numbers'. Error prevention 3: six failure modes, but misses contrast direction, unmodified peptides in $PTM and the R-path localization filter.

human_usability.note: Discoverability 3: natural terms (phosphosites, ubiquitination, regulated) in a dense, jargon-heavy description. Forgiveness 3 (Cat-3 override): input requirements such as the paired global proteome and evidence.txt vs Sites table are stated explicitly.

security.note: No credentials or network use (4); only column-existence guards, no schema validation of user tables (3); local files only, no retention (4).

maintainability.note: Modularity 3: clean sections, but code blocks share variable names across sections. Modifiability 3: named constants (CLASS_I_PROB, WINDOW_HALF); filename and mod hard-coded. Testability 2: the one example uses only aggregated Intensity___n columns, so it never exercises the per-run path where the bug is; nothing covers the R block.

agent_specific.note: Trigger 4: explicit routing to peptide-identification, quantification, differential-abundance and dia-analysis. Disclosure 3: under 500 lines but no references/. Composability 4. Idempotency 4. Escape hatches 3: 'no global proteome -> report UNADJUSTED' and an OUT OF SCOPE list, but no stop for an FLR request without spectra.

key_strengths: The central claim holds when run: MSstatsPTM ADJUSTED.Model removed 6/6 called protein-driven phosphosite changes and 5/5 stabilisation-driven K-GG changes, and recovered masked occupancy changes that PTM.Model missed
Chemistry facts are exact (GG = 2x carbamidomethyl = 114.0429; acetyl/trimethyl delta 0.0364 Da; 18O deglycosylation +2.988), and the references checked against Crossref are genuine
The phospho-only escape hatch is correct: report UNADJUSTED and do not claim regulation
The multiplicity rationale works in practice: expanded ___1/___2 columns exposed a phospho-form switch invisible in the collapsed column
Guidance on experiment-matched motif backgrounds and on prior-limited kinase inference is sound and carried straight into the analysis

recommendations.title: MSstatsPTM block fails as written on 2.8.1
recommendations.problem: dataSummarizationPTM(input, use_log_file = FALSE) fails with "Assertion on '!(append & !use_log_file)' failed". groupComparisonPTM(data.type = 'LF') matches neither branch and stops with "object 'ptm_model' not found".
recommendations.root_cause: The block mixes up the converter's labeling_type = 'LF' with groupComparisonPTM's data.type, and ignores the append = TRUE default.
recommendations.fix: Use dataSummarizationPTM(input, use_log_file = FALSE, append = FALSE) and groupComparisonPTM(summarized, data.type = 'LabelFree'). Add both errors to Common Errors.

recommendations.title: Protein dataset never built: evidence_prot missing
recommendations.problem: The comment says to supply the global proteome, but the call passes only proteinGroups and annotation_protein. MaxQtoMSstatsPTMFormat then returns list(PTM) with no PROTEIN, so no adjustment is possible.
recommendations.root_cause: The code does not match the documented converter contract, which builds $PROTEIN only when evidence_prot is non-NULL.
recommendations.fix: Add evidence_prot = read.table('evidence_global.txt', ...) and which_proteinid_protein = 'Proteins'. Add stopifnot('PROTEIN' %in% names(input)) before summarization.

recommendations.title: Multiplicity melt adds a bogus run named 'Intensity'
recommendations.problem: On a real-format Sites table, mult_cols also matches the aggregated Intensity___1/2/3 columns. The long table gains a 9th 'run' holding the sum over runs: 38 of 295 rows, median 2.74 log2 above the real runs.
recommendations.root_cause: The filter uses c.startswith('Intensity') instead of per-experiment 'Intensity <exp>___n'; the shipped example has only aggregated columns, so it never exposes this.
recommendations.fix: Select with c.startswith('Intensity ') and a ___[123]$ suffix (or exclude ^Intensity___), and add per-run columns to the example.

recommendations.title: R path skips localization filter and keeps unmodified rows
recommendations.problem: In the MSstatsPTM route, class II/III sites are tested (1 with localization prob 0.42 called regulated). Unmodified peptides from the enriched runs enter $PTM as bare-protein 'sites' (39 of 80 rows).
recommendations.root_cause: The class-I rule and the modified-peptide filter exist only in the pandas Sites-table workflow; the converter uses the best-localized sequence as is.
recommendations.fix: Before conversion, keep evidence rows whose Modified sequence matches mod_id and whose max localization probability (parsed from 'Phospho (STY) Probabilities') is >= 0.75. After testing, drop result rows without a site suffix.

recommendations.title: Motif block NameError; no kinase-activity code
recommendations.problem: Run in order, the motif block raises NameError on 'confident'. It defines only a counter, with no background construction or enrichment test. KSEA/PTM-SEA, both promised in the description, have no code.
recommendations.root_cause: The block was lifted from the example, which names the filtered table 'confident', and was never run after the expansion block.
recommendations.fix: Rename to 'phospho'. Add a matched-background builder plus a per-position Fisher/BH test, and a KSEAapp::KSEA.Scores call with a documented PhosphoSitePlus/NetworKIN input and fold-change direction.

recommendations.title: FC+p double filter conflicts with differential-abundance
recommendations.problem: The regulated rule adj.pvalue < 0.05 & abs(log2FC) > 1 is the post-hoc double filter the differential-abundance Skill forbids. In simulation (4v4) it gave 9.1-12.9% false calls for a '>2-fold' claim at nominal 5%.
recommendations.root_cause: The site-level selection rule was not aligned with the sibling Skill's treat-style guidance.
recommendations.fix: Test |log2FC| > c inside the statistic, e.g. p = pt((abs(log2FC) - c)/SE, DF, lower.tail = FALSE) on ADJUSTED.Model, with BH; or call the double filter a ranking heuristic whose FDR refers to FC != 0.

recommendations.title: Default contrast direction is not stated
recommendations.problem: The default pairwise Label is 'Control vs Treatment' (log2FC = Control - Treatment). Downstream KSEA z-scores and up/down calls invert unless the sign is flipped.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill says 'contrast.matrix defaults to full pairwise' without describing the Label orientation.
recommendations.fix: Tell the agent to read adjusted$Label or pass an explicit contrast.matrix (Treatment = 1, Control = -1) before labelling sites up or down.

recommendations.title: FLR and K-GG QC lack a runnable route
recommendations.problem: Reporting an empirical FLR is mandatory, but no route exists from MaxQuant tables. For already-acquired IAA data the only advice is prospective (use chloroacetamide), and C-terminal K-GG IDs pass every filter.
recommendations.root_cause: FLR and diGly guidance are narrative only and assume spectra are available.
recommendations.fix: State that LuciPHOr2/DeepFLR need spectra; otherwise report mean(1 - p) as model-based only. Add a K-GG QC that flags GG on the peptide C-terminal K and asks for the alkylation reagent.

recommendations.title: Phospho-only path: document use_unmod_peptides
recommendations.problem: For phospho-only data the Skill hard-codes use_unmod_peptides = FALSE and never mentions that MSstatsPTM can use co-enriched unmodified peptides as a weak protein proxy.
recommendations.root_cause: Only the paired-proteome route is documented.
recommendations.fix: Add a caveated option: use_unmod_peptides = TRUE when no global run exists, and label the results proxy-adjusted.

recommendations.title: Small doc inconsistencies
recommendations.problem: The filename comment 'accept either form' is not implemented. The example labels Localization prob 0.75 as class II while the filter keeps it as class I. The 'fake dephosphorylation' wording misdescribes the collapse, which masks form switches. Ramsbottom 2022 is cited but not in References.
recommendations.root_cause: Text and code were edited separately.
recommendations.fix: Try both filenames, use right=False bins in the example, reword the multiplicity failure mode, and add Ramsbottom KA et al. J Proteome Res 2022;21(7):1603-1615.
